maria: Heads-up — after the kernel selector change on prod last night we're seeing a small but consistent p95 tail blip across mid-length requests (seq len ~512). looks correlated with bursts where prefill and decode batches hand off.
travis: Can you share the perf summary? p95 number and whether it's CPU/GPU bound?
perf-bot: perf-summary: p95 +11.8% for text-gen route, median unchanged. GPU util steady; scheduler wait time up ~18%. (flame: https://perf.redwood/2061234567)
sloane: I pulled a trace — prefill queue grows then we do an immediate decode handoff which stalls while kv cache warmup serializes. lots of small handoffs.
kevin: Repro locally with stress tool. If handoffs happen more often than every 200ms we incur kernel switch tax + kv page faults. Proposed: add hysteresis window between prefill->decode routing and a staggered batch draining policy.
maria: Sketch of config I tried: 
```
batching:
  prefill:
    token_budget_target: 40
    max_hold_ms: 80
  decode:
    token_budget_target: 8
    handoff_hysteresis_ms: 200
kv_cache:
  warmup_strategy: async_prefill_warmup
```
Kept decode token target low so decodes flush quicker but avoid immediate handoff.
travis: Interesting. Did you measure effect on p95 and throughput?
maria: Quick A/B over a subset of hosts: p95 down ~6% vs baseline, overall throughput stable. But one regression: cold-started sessions (empty KV) saw slightly higher first-token latency.
sloane: That matches the hypothesis — warming KV asynchronously helps steady-state but adds work at first prefill. Could we do a small pre-warm on route assignment? e.g., lightweight KV hinting that doesn't stall the handoff thread.
kevin: Suggestion: implement two-phase warmup: 1) non-blocking touch of KV pages on prefill commit, 2) blocking finish on decode begin only if estimated KV miss rate > 0.25. Also tune handoff_hysteresis_ms per seq-length histogram.
travis: Can you add a perf test in /infra/loadtests that simulates mixed seq lengths and measure handoff_count and kernel_switch_time? Also add a feature-flag gated rollout.
maria: Yep — I'll push a PR with: loadtest + feature flag + basic telemetry for `handoff_hysteresis_ms` and `kv_warmup_mode`. Will iterate on token_budget_target after a few runs.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary hosts apply feature-flag at 15:05 UTC. monitor p95 and handoff_count channels. :eyes:
kevin: Awesome. If we still see micro-regressions I'll try increasing prefill token_budget_target to 48 and reduce decode max_hold_ms to 40 to force smaller decode batches.
maria: Thanks — I'll post the PR and initial canary numbers once available. :thumbsup:
